narrative.overview: A darkened edit suite where only the picture is lit. Every panel around the monitors steps back into neutral graphite so the operator's eye stays on the frame they are cutting; the chrome speaks only when it has to, and then in one colour. The system follows the category standard on purpose, measured against CapCut Desktop and Descript: familiar NLE topology (media pool left, monitors centre, inspector right, multi-track timeline below), executed precisely rather than reinvented.
keyCharacteristics: Neutral graphite ramp; the monitors sit on the darkest ground.
One accent blue: solid fill for the primary action, tinted fill for selection.
Track hues (video, captions, voice, effects, music) live on the timeline only.
Inter for UI, JetBrains Mono for timecodes and measurements.
Flat, hairline-separated surfaces; no glows, gradients-as-decoration or emoji icons.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: Solid Cut Blue appears once per view, on the primary action. Every other accent use is a 15% tint with Cut Blue Text.

rules.name: The Track Hue Fence
rules.body: Track hues never leave the timeline; panels, buttons and chips stay graphite and blue.

rules.name: The No-Glow Rule
rules.body: No zero-offset coloured shadows or glowing text in chrome; caption styling inside the rendered video is content, not chrome.

dos: Do keep the primary action solid Cut Blue (#2563EB) and everything else tinted.
Do set timecodes and durations in JetBrains Mono with tabular figures.
Do use Lucide icons at 14–16px with a consistent stroke.
Do keep secondary text at Ink Muted (#A9ADB4) or brighter.
donts: Don't use emoji as icons in chrome (user-entered titles are content and stay as typed).
Don't introduce a second accent colour or reuse track hues outside the timeline.
Don't add coloured glows, gradient text or coloured side stripes.
